newsitem.title: GERMANY: Official sees German '97 jobless at 4.1-4.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: Official sees German '97 jobless at 4.1-4.2 mln.

text.p: An official at Germany's Federal Labour Office said on Thursday that he expected unemployment to average between 4.1 and 4.2 million this year.
"We expect unemployment to average between 4.1 and 4.2 million in the current year," Eugen Spitznagel, an official in the Labour Office research section, told Reuters.

Spitznagel was speaking after the Labour Office announced record post-war unemployment figures for January. Unadjusted joblessness rose by half a million to 4.66 million from December, while the seasonally adjusted figure climbed by 160,000 to 4.32 million.
He said: "The forecast is based on Germany experiencing relatively strong economic growth. If growth stagnates, the situation could be more serious.
"Looking at economic factors in the core areas of the economy, like manufacturing and building, there seems no prospect of a short-term upturn," he added.

"In the long term, inflation, interest rates and an improvement in the global economy, seem growth-friendly. With the time delay, it will probably be the second half (of 1997) before the impact of growth can be seen on the jobs market."
But, Spitznagel added, economic impulses take time to impact on the jobs market.
Germany's government has based its budget planning on economic growth this year of 2.5 percent and average unemployment of a shade below four million.

Analysts say that higher unemployment could jeopardise Bonn's bid to cut its budget deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product, to meet the Maastricht treaty's three percent deficit goal to qualify for European monetary union in 1999.
